card.name: Dakke Bali
card.tagline: Biennial Tulu serpent-worship ritual dance of Padubidri
card.profile: Dakke Bali is a form of Nagaradhane (serpent worship) practised by the Tulu people of Tulu Nadu, conducted chiefly at the Khadgeshwari Brahmasthana in Padubidri, Udupi district, Karnataka (Wikipedia; Mangalore Heritage). Held once every two years (in years when the Paryaya festival at Udupi does not occur), it runs on certain nights between roughly mid-January and mid-March (Wikipedia). A ritualist dressed as Nagakannika (the half-male/half-female serpent) plays the hourglass-shaped 'dakke' drum to invoke possession in the Patri/Pathri, who then moves in rhythmic circles around an elaborate serpent mandala drawn in natural colours, depicting the divine union of male and female snakes (Mangalore Heritage; The Sunday Guardian).
card.insight: Dakke Bali is, alongside Bhuta Kola, one of the principal ritual dance forms of Tulu Nadu; its nocturnal trance and serpent-mandala worship reflect the region's deep ecological and ancestral reverence for cobras, conducted strictly in lamplight without artificial lighting (Wikipedia; Mangalore Heritage).
